To: page:wensum-valley-hospice-bookshop
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Light Up a Life 2026 (not to be posted until Moira has read it)

Our Light Up a Life tree is in the window again this year, and I have to admit I am slightly emotional about it.

Seven years ago this month, my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag on that tree, I could hardly write it — my hand was all over the place. These days I write it at the counter, with the same pen, while people come and go and the till gets on with it. It takes about as long now as writing a name on an envelope, which is how it ought to be.

The tree is for anybody who is grieving, not only hospice families. If you have lost someone, or someone you love has gone, you are very welcome to come and stand by it. You do not have to buy anything, and you do not have to say anything to anybody. Just come and stand there for a while. Hilary, you asked on here whether we were doing it again — yes we are, and please do bring your sister along. Your mum's name will be read out, as it was last year.

The memory tags are in the shop from Monday 16 November, on the counter, £3 suggested. If you would rather write at home, there are envelopes on the counter for that too.

We switch the lights on at 4pm on Saturday 28 November. Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing us three or four carols, and Doreen is doing the mince pies again, so come in for that alone if nothing else. We will keep it lit until Twelfth Night.

Every name on the tags is read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You do not have to come to the service for your name to be read — it will be read whether you are in the room or not.

Last year the tree carried 412 names, and I want to thank everyone who hung one, whether they wrote it at our counter or at their own kitchen table. That is a great deal of remembering, and it is not a small thing. What the tags paid for went straight back into the hospice's care — most of a month of the night sitter service, which is what we have to offer families at two in the morning.

Thank you. Do come and stand by the tree. Jean
